notes.text: M3 answers whether secrets are current, stale, externally changed, expiring or expired. Provider-side automatic credential rotation is explicitly deferred to M5.

notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: Roadmap renumbered after splitting secure core from runtime secrets; now M4.

problem: After secrets can be delivered and synchronized, developers still lack a reliable view of which versions are stale, what changed outside the system and which credentials require action before expiry.
scope: Extend SecretVersion lifecycle metadata with activation, expiry, revocation and supersession state.
Track desired_version, observed_version when knowable, last_checked_at, last_synced_at and reconciliation status per SyncBinding.
Support synced, pending, failed, stale, expired, drifted and unknown states without overstating what a provider API can verify.
Extend the target-plugin contract with optional inspection/drift capabilities and explicit capability flags.
Add expiry warning windows and views for valid, expiring-soon and expired credentials.
Provide an environment/target matrix showing version, lifecycle and synchronization status.
Expand append-only audit coverage for version activation/revocation, sync and drift events.
Do not create new credentials at providers or automatically revoke provider credentials in M3.
title: Milestone 4: lifecycle, expiry, drift and operational visibility
validation: A user can identify all credentials expiring within a configured warning window.
The UI/API can distinguish intentional pinning, stale desired state, provider drift and unverifiable/unknown state.
A plugin that cannot read secret values can still report its real inspection capabilities without core assuming plaintext comparison.
The environment matrix identifies the desired/current secret version per target wherever the provider permits it.
Audit events never contain secret plaintext.
value: Make secret lifecycle operationally visible so teams know what is stale, what expires next and where configuration has drifted.
